title: DSPy and GEPA Prompt Optimization: A Self-Improving Fact Checker
summary: Julian Ghadially shows how DSPy and GEPA tune prompts from an evaluation dataset instead of by hand.
learn: Prompt optimization works well when you have ground-truth labels: the dataset does the work of writing the prompt.
GEPA (Genetic Pareto) mutates and merges prompts and keeps a Pareto frontier; a reflective model sees traces, outputs and feedback to propose new prompts.
He cites researchers reporting about a 20% gain on multi-hop question-answering datasets, beating reinforcement learning.
In DSPy you write signatures instead of prompts and build modules like Predict, ChainOfThought and ReAct from them.
His fact checker, an iterative judge with a research agent, went from 91% to 96% accuracy on predicted cases, about half the errors.
